research_problem: REST API fuzzers detect crashes and schema mismatches but not authorization faults (BOLA/BFLA); access policies are never formally specified
technical_approach: Post-fuzzing security phase in EvoMaster: reuse and slice fuzzer-generated tests with multiple users to instantiate scenarios for three status-code-based oracles: Not-Recognized (401 for authenticated user), Leakage (403 vs 404 existence disclosure), Missed-Check (403 on one of PUT/PATCH/DELETE but 2xx on another)
primary_contribution: Three specification-free automated access-policy oracles integrated into a REST fuzzer
dataset_benchmark: 3 artificial APIs with injected faults; 3 security example APIs (capital, crAPI, WebGoat); 10 authenticated EMB real-world APIs (291K LoC, 792 endpoints)
evaluation_metrics: Average distinct faults per oracle over 10 runs, compared with existing H500 and schema oracles
key_findings: All injected faults found; 27 distinct new faults overall (Not-Recognized 22.2, Leakage 3.0, Missed-Check 0.7 average sums); Missed-Check only in capital, none in real-world APIs; existing oracles report 812 500s and 12,413 schema faults whose severity is questionable
author_limitations: 16 APIs; integration into other fuzzers untested; depends on fuzzer-generated tests; Missed-Check false positives possible; recall not assessed; severity unknown without practitioners
analyst_limitations: Precision never measured and no developer confirmation; most findings are usability (401) faults not vulnerabilities; true BOLA (cross-user 2xx) not directly detected; inconsistent '13 real-world' count; self-evaluation, no cross-tool comparison; 200-with-error-body APIs confuse status oracles
reproducibility: High: open-source EvoMaster extension and public SUTs
suggested_extensions: Ownership tracking and LLM policy inference for direct BOLA oracles; practitioner-validated precision/severity study; cross-tool REST security oracle benchmark; LLM-assisted fault triage; response-semantic oracles
evidence_location: Oracles p.3-6; integration p.6-7; RQs/setup p.8; Table III p.9; discussion p.11; threats p.11
integrity: Two-column interleaving in oracle sections; tables column-split but verified via Sum row
